narrative:
The service corridor shuddered as the outer gate took another hit. Water ticked through a cracked pipe into the bucket between Mara and Iven, each drop loud enough to measure the time they had left. Iven held the stolen access seal in his fist. “You always did prefer doors that opened for you,” he said. The joke was almost light; his thumb kept rubbing the blood from its edge.

Mara reached for the seal. He closed his hand around it and stepped back. Beyond him, boots scraped over the grate. If the wardens found him carrying it, they would take him first. Mara could let them. He had not asked why the patrol had missed her at the checkpoint, and she had not told him whose name she had used to make that happen.

“Give me the seal,” she said. “I can get you out.”

“Out to where?”

“To the west stairs.”

“An ambitious promise from someone who brought me a locked door.”

The next impact bent the corridor light sideways. Mara flinched toward the sound, then forced her hand still. Iven noticed. His smile thinned. “You could say it,” he said.

She looked at the blood on his palm instead. “I can carry you as far as the stairs.”

“That is not what I asked.”

“No.” Her voice stayed flat. “It is what I’m offering.”

For a moment, he held the seal out—not to her, but over the drain. “Then swear you won’t trade me for your own passage.”

Mara’s eyes went to the rising water. The drain was clogging with plaster. “If I swear, you’ll call it another bargain.”

“I’ll call it an improvement.”

She took off her coat and pressed it against the pipe’s leaking joint, sacrificing the only dry layer between them and the cold. With her free hand, she unlatched the emergency grille. The mechanism seized. Iven could have kept the seal and run when she failed. Instead, he braced his injured shoulder against the grille and pushed.

The latch gave. Mara caught him before he fell, then shoved the seal into his hand. “West stairs,” she said. “When we reach them, we separate.”

He studied her, breathing hard. “You forgot the part where you say you’re sorry.”

“I’m saving it until you can afford to believe me.”

He almost laughed. Together they passed through the grille as the gate buckled behind them. Iven kept the seal; Mara kept her hand beneath his elbow. Neither called it trust, but neither let go.
title: The Price of Staying Quiet
